jobs.title: Sr. Director, Engineering - Digital Video & Audio (DVA)
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Adobe's Digital Video & Audio (DVA) business powers the world's leading creative tools for professional video editing, motion graphics, visual effects, and content creation. Premiere Pro and After Effects are industry-defining applications used by filmmakers, broadcasters, social creators, enterprises, and creative professionals worldwide!

The future of creative storytelling will be hybrid, bringing together traditional craft and AI-powered creation in ways that expand what's possible. Whether an artist starts with an ARRI camera, a script, or a prompt, Adobe is building the world's leading creative platform to support every stage of the journey. From intelligent editing and generative video to cloud-native workflows and connected creative experiences, Digital Video & Audio is helping creators imagine, craft, and deliver compelling stories wherever inspiration begins.

As Senior Director of Engineering, you will lead engineering strategy and execution across Premiere Pro, After Effects, and the platform, helping shape the future of professional video creation. You will partner closely across Product, Design, Research, and Platform Engineering to accelerate innovation, modernize core technologies, and deliver intelligent experiences that delight millions of creators around the world.

This is a highly visible leadership role supporting one of Adobe's most strategic product portfolios. Success requires building high-performing teams, influencing across a complex matrixed organization, and driving technical and organizational excellence at scale.

You will partner closely with leaders across Product Management, Design, Applied Research, Firefly AI, Creative Cloud, and Engineering to define and deliver the future of Adobe's video, motion graphics, and creative technology platform.

We are looking for an experienced engineering leader with strong technical judgment, operational rigor, and a track record of delivering creative products through major technology shifts. The ideal candidate has modernized mature architectures, scaled organizations, and integrated AI into customer experiences at global scale.

What You’ll Do

Define and drive the engineering strategy for DVA across. Lead the next generation of AI-native and agent-based creative experiences.
Integrate generative AI, intelligent agents, and multimodal workflows into creator experiences in partnership with Adobe AI Research and Firefly teams.
Lead engineering execution and advance extensibility frameworks, developer experiences, and AI-powered workflows while delivering seamless experiences across devices and creative surfaces.
Drive the technology strategy for Adobe's Digital Video & Audio portfolio, accelerating AI-powered experiences across Premiere Pro, After Effects, and the platform. Modernize core video and rendering technologies, cloud services, collaboration capabilities, extensibility frameworks, and shared platform infrastructure while balancing architectural transformation with continuous product delivery.
Build and develop a high performing global engineering organization responsible for performance, scalability, reliability, and operational rigor. Foster accountability, technical excellence, innovation, and strong execution while partnering across Adobe to align strategy, priorities, and platform direction.
Represent Adobe externally through executive engagement, technical leadership, and a clear vision for shaping the next era of creativity.

What You'll Need To Succeed

Demonstrated ownership of business outcomes that delivered double-digit growth. Experience expanding product value and adoption among new and emerging creators, with a strong focus on activation, retention, and business impact.
15+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping products with a worldwide reach. Experience leading large distributed engineering organizations responsible for complex, business-critical platforms including large-scale desktop applications and cross-platform experiences used by millions of creators.
Proven experience integrating AI and machine learning technologies to enhance customer experiences, including generative AI, large language models, agent-based workflows, orchestration frameworks, inference systems, and multimodal experiences.
Demonstrated success in modernizing platforms and leading large-scale AI adoption initiatives across mature engineering organizations and codebases. Experience improving engineering productivity through AI-assisted development and modern delivery practices.
Strong technical depth across native applications, cloud-connected platforms, distributed systems, web, mobile, AI infrastructure, and developer ecosystems.
Deep understanding of scalability, reliability, performance optimization, platform architecture, and operational excellence. Experience supporting globally distributed products and services used at large scale.
Passion for creativity tools and a strong understanding of creator workflows, imaging technologies, graphics systems, extensibility, security, compliance, and enterprise requirements.
Proven ability to build and develop leadership teams across directors, managers, architects, and engineers. Experience driving alignment across executive collaborators and partnering with organizations such as Premiere, Illustrator, and Firefly to deliver connected creative workflows.
Exceptional communication, organizational leadership, and influence skills. Ability to inspire teams, shape strategy, and lead significant organizational change.

About Adobe

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.

Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours.

Let’s Adobe together

At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture, focus on people, purpose and community, Adobe for All, comprehensive benefits programs, the stories we tell, the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create.

Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more.

jobs.title: Director, Power Generation Operations (on-site Doña Ana County, NM)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

We are seeking an experienced Director, Fuel Cell & Power Generation Operations
to lead the operation, reliability, and continuous improvement of on-site power generation supporting mission-critical data center infrastructure.

This role will have operational responsibility for fuel cell systems serving as a primary source of on-site power
, along with backup and emergency generator systems
and associated electrical and balance-of-plant infrastructure.

A strong understanding of fuel cell technology, operating characteristics, controls, maintenance requirements, and system integration
is critical to success in this role. The Director will establish the teams, operating practices, maintenance strategies, and technical procedures necessary to safely operate these assets while maintaining continuous protection of critical compute load.

The ideal candidate brings leadership experience from fuel cell operations, fuel cell technology or service organizations, mission-critical power operations, or power generation environments with direct fuel cell experience
. This leader will also play a key role in commissioning new generation assets and establishing a scalable operating model as our on-site power generation capabilities grow.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, develop, and scale teams responsible for the operation and maintenance of fuel cell power generation systems, backup and emergency generators, and associated electrical and balance-of-plant infrastructure.
Provide technical and operational leadership for fuel cell systems, including equipment performance, operating characteristics, controls, maintenance requirements, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management.
Establish operating strategies that maximize fuel cell availability, reliability, and performance while ensuring continuous protection of mission-critical compute load.
Develop, document, test, and continuously improve Methods of Procedure (MOPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs), and maintenance procedures.
Establish procedures to safely manage generation transitions, load transfers, ramp events, equipment outages, utility events, and other normal and abnormal operating conditions.
Partner with engineering, commissioning, data center operations, training, and technology providers to develop effective technical qualification, repair, preventive maintenance, and training programs.
Lead operational readiness, commissioning, acceptance, and turnover of new fuel cell generation assets and associated electrical infrastructure.
Develop maintenance strategies using equipment condition, operating history, manufacturer requirements, and performance data to maximize generation availability and reliability.
Establish, monitor, and report performance metrics for system availability, reliability, efficiency, equipment health, maintenance effectiveness, and incident response.
Manage operational relationships and agreements with fuel cell technology providers, service organizations, generator providers, utilities, and other critical partners.
Recruit, hire, develop, and retain specialized operations and maintenance personnel with the technical capabilities required to support fuel cell and backup generation systems.
Serve as the senior operational escalation point for high-severity generation incidents, coordinating troubleshooting, recovery, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions.
Champion a culture of safety, operational discipline, compliance, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Maintain knowledge of emerging fuel cell and power generation technologies, operating practices, and regulatory requirements relevant to mission-critical facilities.

Responsibilities

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Energy Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant technical and operational experience.
Significant experience operating, maintaining, commissioning, engineering, or technically supporting fuel cell power generation systems.
Strong working knowledge of fuel cell technology and its application in continuous power generation environments.
Demonstrated understanding of fuel cell operating characteristics, balance-of-plant systems, controls, maintenance practices, failure modes, and equipment performance.
Experience integrating primary generation systems with critical electrical loads and backup/emergency generation.
Demonstrated leadership experience building and developing technical operations, maintenance, field service, or engineering teams.
Experience establishing operating procedures, maintenance programs, technical qualification programs, and operational readiness processes.
Demonstrated ability to lead troubleshooting and operational decision-making in high-availability environments.
Strong safety mindset and experience operating within structured environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills with the ability to work effectively across operations, engineering, commissioning, technology providers, utilities, and business organizations.

Highly Relevant Experience

Experience in several of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

Fuel cell technology and power generation
Fuel cell operations and maintenance
Fuel cell field service or technical operations
Fuel cell installation and commissioning
Fuel cell balance-of-plant systems
Natural gas systems supporting fuel cell generation
Generation controls, SCADA, and power monitoring systems
Mission-critical electrical infrastructure
Data center power operations
Backup and emergency generator systems
Commissioning and operational turnover of new power infrastructure
High-availability power generation environments

Preferred Qualifications

Leadership experience within a fuel cell technology, power generation, field service, or technical operations organization.
Significant hands-on or leadership experience with fuel cell systems, including operations, maintenance, troubleshooting, commissioning, or field service.
Experience managing technology-provider maintenance and service relationships and driving equipment reliability improvements.
Experience operating primary on-site generation alongside backup and emergency generator systems.
Experience integrating on-site generation with utility service and mission-critical electrical infrastructure.
Familiarity with CMMS, SCADA, power monitoring, and generation control systems.
Knowledge of applicable OSHA, EPA, utility, and power-generation regulatory requirements.
Experience building or scaling an operations organization during commissioning and ramp-up of a new facility.

Location

This position is located onsite -Doña Ana County, New Mexico. Relocation to a daily commutable location is required for this role.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Core Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

This position is based at our Nashville, TN location.

Manages team delivering scalable distributed systems and components on a 2–4 quarter horizon. Standardizes engineering practices and scalability requirements across teams; oversees optimization for high‑throughput, hyper‑scale workloads; and ensures effective use of distributed state tools and data plane platforms. Guides teams to design fault‑tolerant, in‑service‑upgradable systems, set SLO‑aligned durability/availability targets, and implement resiliency mechanisms (load‑shedding, throttling, rate‑limiting). Provides oversight for KPIs, telemetry, and moderately complex dashboards; directs design of functional/correctness requirements, fault‑injection tests, and replication/synchronization strategies. Ensures proactive incident management, operational readiness, and on‑call coverage; drives encryption/access control practices, remediation plans, and compliance documentation. Oversees development and maintenance of automation/IaC and partners with teams on change‑management plans enabling safe patching, updates, and rollbacks.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

System Design & Architecture – System Scalability:

Manages the development and implementation of scalable distributed systems and components across multiple teams, including the effective use of distributed state management tools.
Oversees code and/or system optimization efforts for large-scale data processing and high-throughput requirements within and across teams to support hyper-scale systems.
Guides teams to define scalability requirements for owned components and ensures design and implementation requirements are met.
Manages the use of data plane platforms to effectively handle large-scale data retrieval, storage, and processing.
Ensures team accurately designs performance and load testing.

System Design & Architecture – System Reliability Design:

Manages the strategy for building fault-tolerant components and systems capable of withstanding in-service updates by guiding the implementation of redundancy, replication, and automatic failover mechanisms.
Develops design strategies for systems to effectively handle service disruptions (e.g., network partitions) by prioritizing consistency, availability, or partition tolerance.
Leads implementation and optimization initiatives across teams for approaches to handle network unreliability, including load-shedding, throttling, and rate-limiting.
Guides teams to design components and systems that are durable and adhere to service level objectives (SLOs), setting expectations for availability and durability of other computing services within the department.

System Design & Architecture – System Reliability Performance:

Provides oversight in defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and telemetry to identify gaps or issues in running systems.
Oversees the building and customization of moderately complex dashboards, telemetry systems, and alerting mechanisms to proactively monitor components and system health.

System Design & Architecture – Correctness / Availability:

Oversees the design and implementation of functional and correctness requirements for feature sets and/or systems in new or existing systems.
Guides teams to design complex test scenarios (e.g., fault-injection, brown-out) to evaluate system correctness.
Directs implementation strategies for data replication and synchronization techniques to maintain data integrity and availability.

Operational Troubleshooting & Incident Management:

Guides teams to be proactive when diagnosing, debugging, and resolving issues in active components and systems to support ongoing operation.
Ensures teams leverage expertise to prevent interruptions, ensuring no maintenance windows are required for customers and users when resolving issues.
Oversees operational readiness protocol and ensures teams remain knowledgeable of owned components and systems to support effective troubleshooting and performance.
Oversees and approves schedules for operational support rotations.

Compliance & Security:

Oversees implementation of robust security measures to protect data and applications in multi-tenant environments, ensuring team strategies incorporate encryption techniques and access controls.
Directs execution of remediation plans to address identified security gaps, promoting continuous improvement of security measures.
Ensures comprehensive documentation and cloud infrastructure compliance with industry standards and regulations.

Automation & Change Management:

Oversees the development and maintenance of automation scripts and tools (e.g., Infrastructure as Code (IaC)) to manage cloud infrastructure.
Works with teams to create and adhere to change management plans for patching, updating, and rolling back applications, and guides development of components to allow for automation of these processes.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

Manages multiple medium- to large-scale projects or initiatives across teams, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and budgets (when applicable) are monitored and met.
Provides direction to teams on project work, setting priorities, and aligning with business needs.
Guides teams on adjusting plans to accommodate resource or timeline changes.

Collaboration & Partnership:

Drives cross-functional partnerships to align on expectations and shared objectives across multiple teams.
Coaches team members to develop strategic relationships with business leaders, stakeholders, and external partners to foster collaboration and long-term success.
Promotes inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

Provides direction to multiple teams on addressing complex operational and/or technical issues, as well as guidance on analyzing complex data and/or information to identify solutions.
Reviews and provides insights into unresolved or critical issues, helping teams to identify potential solutions.

Continuous Learning:

Models engaging in continuous learning to deepen expertise and stay ahead of industry trends, integrating best practices into strategic planning.
Leverages feedback to drive personal and team skill improvements.
Identifies skill gaps across teams and empowers team members to pursue learning and knowledge-sharing opportunities that build their expertise in new areas, coaching them to apply learnings to advance the organization.

Continuous Improvement:

Drives teams to collaborate on, develop, and implement ideas to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within and across teams, providing oversight.
Guides teams to adopt new ideas for alternative approaches and methods and encourages feedback for continued improvement.

Performance and Development:

Drives performance across teams by providing feedback and coaching in alignment with performance management processes, guidelines, and expectations.
Discusses development goals with team members, shares opportunities to facilitate career development, and ensures individual goals are aligned with broader organizational goals.
Develops and manages talent acquisition pipeline by leading candidate interviews, monitoring promotion eligibility, and/or orchestrating talent resources.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager for Self-Serve (Learning)
jobs.description:
RDQ426R220

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.

The Self-Serve team owns Databricks' product-led growth motion — the experience that takes someone from "I just heard about Databricks" to succeeding on the platform entirely on their own. Our most ambitious bet is Learning: making Databricks the place where anyone interested in data + AI comes to learn, and building the largest community of active, capable learners in the world. It's a long game with a simple thesis — if people learn data + AI on Databricks, it becomes ubiquitous with the field itself, driving adoption and revenue.

As a Senior Engineering Manager on the Self-Serve team, you will lead the Learning bet end to end across two sides: self-paced learning — a place to learn any Databricks skill, hands-on labs that spin up inside a real workspace, and a durable skill profile a learner carries across jobs — and enterprise-managed learning, giving admins the tools to assign, track, and grow learning inside their orgs. AI is central to both: a content-generation agent that scales the catalog far past what we could author by hand, and an AI tutor that guides learners hands-on inside the product. This is a genuine 0→1 product with real systems depth — on-demand provisioning, identity, sandboxing, and an interactive learning engine that must scale to millions of learners — and you'll grow and lead a team of ~12 engineers (planned to roughly double) to build it.

The Impact You Will Have

Strategy & Vision: Define and drive the technical and product strategy for Learning, and tie it into the broader self-serve growth motion.
Execution Ownership: Own the roadmap, execution, and delivery — taking a 0→1 product from early signal to millions of learners at the highest standards of quality.
Engineering Excellence: Establish team best practices — design reviews, code quality, testing, and performance for high-scale, interactive systems.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely across R&D, the Learning & Enablement org, Marketing (university and online channels), and Field Engineering to align the product with how learners actually reach and adopt Databricks.

What We Look For

Experience:
15+ years of software engineering experience with a strong track record of technical leadership and impact.
5+ years of engineering management experience, including 2+ years managing other managers (or clear readiness to).

Technical Depth: A Staff engineer caliber IC background before pivoting to management, with full-stack experience (including back-end, not purely front-end/UI); comfort leading a mix of front-end and full-stack engineers.
Scaling: Proven experience scaling engineering teams from 10 to 30+ engineers.
Product & Domain Fit:
A track record building and scaling consumer-facing products, ideally taking early-stage products from 0→1 through scale. Scope- and impact-driven over team-size-driven.
Genuine excitement for product-led growth and putting AI to work in a real product.

Systems at scale: Experience designing scalable, distributed, customer-facing systems, ideally in a SaaS environment.
Collaboration: Strong ability to align technical strategy with company growth objectives across product, engineering, and go-to-market partners.

The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, relevant certifications and training, and specific work location. Based on the factors above, Databricks anticipates utilizing the full width of the range. The total compensation package for this position may also include eligibility for annual performance bonus, equity, and the benefits listed above. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering - Web (Ads Customer Interface)
jobs.description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.  
Roku is changing how the world watches TV
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

What is the role? In this role you will work as a key member of the Roku Ads Engineering Customer Interface (ACI) team. You will hire and develop a team that will design, develop, and operate components of our best-in-class suite of customer-facing web applications including Campaign Management, Demand Side Platform, Data Management Platform, Reporting and Forecasting toolsets. The customer interface team and the corresponding API services layer operate on a modern tech stack including React, Node.js and agentic AI technologies.
How will I use AI at Roku?
At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. Horizon Catalog & Metadata: Building agentic experiences for exploring/understanding all the data estate and expressing governance intent, governance capabilities like data-quality monitoring and lineage tracking and integration with open standards (such as Apache Polaris / Iceberg REST catalog).
Collaboration & Marketplace: Building the sharing, application, and commerce platforms (Secure Data Sharing, Zero Copy, Native Apps, Data Clean Rooms, and Snowflake Marketplace) that connect providers and consumers across organizations, clouds, and regions.

Power Enterprise Administration & Control: Architect administrative tooling, tenant management control planes, and centralized policy orchestration that make managing Snowflake across hundreds of accounts and global regions simple and foolproof.
Scale Collaboration & Marketplace: Lead the platforms behind secure data sharing, zero-copy partner integrations, Data Clean Rooms, and Snowflake Marketplace, the network that lets thousands of organizations share and monetize data, applications, and AI products across clouds and regions.
Drive Cross-Functional Alignment: Collaborate closely with Product Management (PM), Design, and Security leaders to translate enterprise customer pain points into high-velocity execution roadmaps.
Customer & Operational Leadership: Serve as an executive sponsor for tier-1 enterprise customers; champion operational excellence, security-by-design, and 99.99%+ availability across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

Experience: 15+ years of software engineering experience in product infrastructure, distributed systems, or enterprise cloud platforms, including 7+ years managing engineering directors, managers, and senior leaders across multi-team organizations.
Product-Minded Engineering Leadership: Strong technical product acumen: you don't just build infrastructure in a vacuum. You deeply understand customer workflows, the enterprise admin persona, usability, and how technical architecture drives product adoption.
Distributed Systems at Scale: Strong foundation in cloud-native distributed systems, high-throughput metadata storage, query execution, caching layers, and cross-region replication.

jobs.title: Chief Engineers, Advanced Aircraft Programs
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Air Dominance and Strike (AD&S) Chief Engineering Team is the technical authority for our most critical programs. They are responsible for owning the technical baseline, leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams through rigorous development and flight test, and delivering revolutionary airborne systems that meet the mission. They are the ultimate problem-solvers, driving technical execution from architecture to operational demonstration.

About The Job

Anduril is looking for strong technical leaders to spearhead the development of new capabilities for new customers. You will own the technical development from concept refinement through detailed design, build, flight test, and transition to production for a new aircraft concept. These projects require you to leverage your deep technical expertise and leadership skills to set objectives, build a team, and deliver real products on a rapid timeline, balancing risk and execution speed without being bound by unnecessary process. We have multiple Chief Engineer and Deputy Chief Engineer opportunities available across a range of advanced platforms.

We will work with exceptional candidates to find the best fit for their unique expertise.

The Leader Of Leaders

Chief Engineer, Next Gen Airpower - You will serve as the technical authority for a 5th or 6th generation multi-role platform, with a focus on integrating survivability and advanced mission systems into a next-generation air dominance solution.
Chief Engineer, High Speed - You will lead the development of a Mach 3+ air vehicle, leveraging deep expertise in high-speed aerodynamics, air-breathing or rocket propulsion, and the high-temperature materials required for extreme flight regimes.
Chief Engineer, Large Autonomous Aircraft - You will own the development of a large-scale autonomous aircraft (over 150,000 lbs GTOW), tackling the unique structural, aerodynamic, and endurance challenges of HALE or large-payload platforms.
Chief Engineer, Navy Airpower - You will own the technical development of a carrier-based autonomous aircraft, with a deep, proven emphasis on carrier suitability, naval aviation requirements, and the NAVAIR airworthiness process.
Chief Engineer, Conventional ISR - You will lead the full EMD of a Group 3+ ISR and/or strike platform, with a special emphasis on integrating the complex sensors, payloads, data links, and mission systems that define the aircraft's capability.
Chief Engineer, Next-Gen ISR- You will lead a low-observable ISR/strike program where "exquisite survivability" is the primary design driver, making the integrated trades between signature, performance, and mission systems
Chief Engineer, Advanced Development - You are a proven "builder" who can lead the hands-on prototyping and integration of a new complex aerospace vehicle.
Chief Engineer, Advanced Concepts - You are responsible for inventing, designing, building, and testing new versions and new capabilities for Anduril's "Fury" unmanned aircraft system.

Required Qualifications

Proven "Cradle-to-Flight" Ownership: You have served as the Chief Engineer, Air Vehicle IPT Lead, or equivalent single point of technical authority on at least one clean-sheet or major-variant aircraft program, and you saw it through from the conceptual design phase to a successful flight test campaign.
Cross-Disciplinary Technical Authority: You have a demonstrated history of personally making and owning the integrated technical trades between at least three of the following core disciplines: Aerodynamics, Structures, Propulsion, GNC, or Systems Integration. You are not a career-long specialist in a single area.
EMD "Valley of Death" Experience: You have led a multi-disciplinary team through the chaos of a first-article build, integration, and ground test. You have personally dispositioned MRB tags, solved integration problems on the shop floor, and held "red-line authority" to keep the build moving.
"Builder" DNA: Your career shows a clear pattern of prioritizing hardware over slide decks. You have a healthy skepticism of analysis-paralysis and a demonstrated ability to make decisions with incomplete information to maintain schedule velocity.
First-Principles Knowledge: You possess a deep, intuitive understanding of the "why" behind aircraft design, rooted in a Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline (Aerospace, Mechanical preferred) or an equivalent track record of shipping complex hardware.
Clearance: You must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct Unmanned Combat/Tactical Aircraft Experience: You were a senior technical leader on a program like the MQ-25, X-47B, B-21, NGAD, CCA-class platforms, or other classified advanced UAS.
Prior experience with DoD technology development organizations (e.g., DARPA, AFRL) on advanced flight programs.
You have a background in an organization known for rapid, innovative, and successful aircraft development, such as Skunk Works, Phantom Works, Scaled Composites, or a high-performance startup environment.
Full Airworthiness & Certification Experience: You have not just supported, but have been a key leader in taking an aircraft through a full military or FAA type certification process, including direct engagement with authorities like NAVAIR or the FAA.
"Fly/No-Fly" Authority: You have been in the control room as the final engineering authority making the "go/no-go" decision for a first flight or a high-risk test point.
Customer & CONOPS Experience: You have worked directly with senior military customers (O-6, Flag Officer, or SES level) to define a new Concept of Operations (CONOPS) and translate it into a technical solution and a funded program.
Specific Domain Expertise (for specialized roles)
Navy: Deep, personal experience with carrier suitability, arrested landings, and NAVAIR standards.
Low Observable: A background where you were the technical authority for signature management (RCS/IR) and survivability trades.
High Speed: Proven leadership on a Mach 3+ program with expertise in aerothermal effects and advanced propulsion.

Active TS/SCI Clearance: You currently hold a high-level clearance, enabling you to engage on our most sensitive programs from day one.

Per Anduril's expansion plans, we anticipate these jobs will be based out of Long Beach, CA beginning late 2027.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

About The Role

Roblox Studio is the creation engine behind millions of immersive 3D games built by creators around the world. We are entering a major platform transition, evolving Studio into an AI-Native IDE where intelligent systems plan, act, validate, and iterate alongside creators to amplify their output. We are seeking a Technical Director, Applied AI to own the technical direction of the agentic AI systems embedded deeply into Roblox Studio. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role operating at the intersection of platform engineering, AI systems, and developer experience, where you will set the technical direction, design the architecture, and write the code.

You Will

Design and build the agentic AI systems at the core of the AI-Native IDE (planning, execution, validation, evaluation) so they are production-grade and reliable.
Decide how Studio uses coding models, agents, retrieval, tool calling, and context management across the Assistant and the broader creator workflow.
Own the quality bar and evaluation strategy, standing up quantitative and qualitative eval pipelines, including human-in-the-loop, so we ship with confidence.
Optimize these systems for latency, throughput, and cost (caching, routing, distillation, quantization).
Bring reusable patterns and best practices to teams across Studio, raising the applied-AI fluency of Studio engineering.

You Have

12+ years of engineering experience, including ownership of large-scale, long-lived platforms.
Deep, hands-on experience building LLM-powered and agentic systems in production, beyond chat-based interfaces.
Strong systems and software engineering skills, with the ability to design the architecture and write the code.
A track record of defining evaluation frameworks for AI product quality, combining automated metrics with human review, and optimizing inference for latency, throughput, and cost.
Strong background in developer tools or IDE-like platforms, with a proven ability to set technical direction and raise quality across multiple teams as an individual contributor.

An innovative technical leader who wants to build the AI systems that power the creativity of millions.
Product-minded, with a real understanding of developer needs, creator workflows, and how AI systems land in the user experience.

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

Anduril's Maritime Division is responsible for planning and executing Anduril's product and revenue roadmap for maritime missions. Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, and operations, the Maritime team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains the Anduril maritime capabilities in a challenging operational environment worldwide. As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success.

About The Job

You will lead the technical development and integration as Chief Engineer
for a maritime product, from initial concept through delivery. You will work closely with program leadership, teams from other Anduril products, and third party system vendors to develop these engineering solutions so that requirements are tied to customer inputs and there is traceability to program office technical decisions.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

What You'll Do

Support early architecture definition and scoping for a new product, defining the technical approach, key requirements, and prototype design
Support the build out of development timelines with associated milestones and staffing needs
Work directly with the product team (Product Manager, EPM, Lead Systems Engineer) to ensure tactical development is executed on plan
Accountable for technical decisions and developments on the AUV

Lead a new team within Anduril Maritime working on development and prototyping of a new platform; defining key performance parameters and requirements and supporting SRR, PDR, and CDR
Work closely with functional leads to drive common approaches for technical development and process

Key stakeholder for technical feasibility/impact in proposed work or capability insertion

Deep understanding of ocean-going craft, systems engineering, product development, and overall engineering process
Experience in a senior role leading maritime programs from initial concept through test and delivery to customers
Strong understanding of the "why" behind vehicle and systems design

Experience creating teams and focusing them around a common vision, leading by example and embodying high-ownership over the problem and the technical solution

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager - Agent Platform, AI Platform
jobs.description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence powers innovation in all areas of the business, from helping members choose the right entertainment for them through personalization, to better understanding our audience and our content slate, to optimizing our payment processing and other revenue-focused initiatives. Building highly scalable and differentiated ML infrastructure is key to accelerating this innovation.

The Opportunity

Agents are becoming a primary way software gets built and work gets done at Netflix — and the AI Platform is building the foundation they run on. The Agent Platform team owns the agent-specific layer that every agent at Netflix depends on: the runtime and execution environment, memory, identity and permissioning, discovery and registry, evaluation, and the tool/MCP interfaces agents use to act. We build the paved path agent developers across the company build on, and we operate the runtimes for the workloads the general platform can't reach — including at member scale.

We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead this team. This is a small, senior, high-leverage group working at the front edge of a domain that is still being invented — where frameworks turn over in months and the durable bets are not obvious. The hardest part of this job is not the code — it is choosing what to build, and what will still matter once today's tools are gone.

You Will

Own the charter and technical direction. Set the platform's technical strategy and roadmap — the agent-specific foundation every agent depends on, and the selective runtimes worth operating directly — and decide where to invest ahead of demand.
Lead and grow a high performing team. Hire, develop, and retain excellent engineers; set a high bar; and create the conditions for a small team to have outsized impact.
Make sharp build, adopt, or partner calls. Decide which capabilities the platform owns and which it draws from partner teams, define the interfaces between them, and keep a small team focused on the highest-leverage layer.
Turn the new hard problems into primitives. The most durable problems in this space are the ones that let agents get better from their own experience: capturing each run's full reasoning-and-tool-call trajectory as structured, replayable data; turning real-world outcomes into evaluation signal; memory that compounds across runs; and a feedback loop that turns that signal into improved behavior, promoted behind eval gates and safe rollout. Make these first-class platform capabilities with real contracts — so agents built on the platform measurably improve over time, not just scale.
Operate as part of the AI Platform leadership team. Set direction alongside peer leaders across the AI Platform and partner orgs, represent the team in senior technical forums, and build the cross-team alignment a foundational platform depends on.

If you've built platforms and you know that the defining work is judgment — what to own, what to hand off, what to bet on while the ground is still moving — this is the role.

Minimum Qualifications

Experience leading and growing engineering teams that build and operate platform or infrastructure at scale — managing senior individual contributors and/or managers, with a track record of developing strong engineers.
Hands-on experience designing, building, and operating agentic systems in production — agent runtimes and harnesses, tool use, memory, and evaluation — with genuine technical depth, not oversight from a distance.
Breadth across business applications: you've built or led agents spanning a range of use cases, enterprise and internal applications (developer tooling, operations, knowledge work) or consumer-facing applications at scale.
A strong engineering foundation in distributed systems, cloud, and ML/AI infrastructure — deep enough to lead a senior team's hardest architectural decisions and earn its trust.
A track record of owning a platform's charter — setting its direction and holding its scope against pressure to do everything — and making build-versus-partner decisions on a multi-year cost horizon.
Cross-organizational credibility: a record of building shared accountability with senior leaders across adjacent platform, infrastructure, and security teams, and navigating ambiguous ownership boundaries.
Strong written and verbal communication; comfort with ambiguity; able to lead both 0-to-1 and 1-to-100 work; effective across a distributed (US) team.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with the emerging class of agent concerns: agent identity and permissioning, guardrails and safety, and cost governance for LLM and agent workloads.
Experience running a platform that other engineers consume as a product — paved paths, migrations, deprecations, and developer experience.
Credibility in a relevant open-source ecosystem (agent frameworks, runtimes, or developer tooling).

To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $676,000.00 - $1,195,000.00. This compensation range will vary based on location.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering - Robotics Manipulation
jobs.description:
NVIDIA is the engine of modern AI, and robotics is where AI meets the physical world. The Isaac robotics platform — spanning Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac ROS, the foundation models behind Isaac GR00T, and the accelerated libraries that run on Jetson and in the data center — is how the world’s developers and industrial leaders build intelligent robots.

We are looking for an exceptional engineering leader and manager to head up Isaac for Manipulation: giving robotic arms and dexterous systems the perception, grasping, motion, and learned skills they need to do real, impactful work. You will be responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and execution for Manipulation — turning hard, contact-rich problems in manufacturing, logistics, and industrial automation into shipping capabilities that our partners and developers can build on. This is a high-visibility role with direct line of sight to the most consequential problems in robotics today. You will grow and mentor a team of world-class robotics and machine-learning engineers, set a bold technical direction, and partner deeply with the robot-arm and industrial-automation ecosystem to make NVIDIA the default platform for robotic manipulation.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead the Isaac Manipulation team. Recruit, grow, and mentor a high-performing team of robotics software engineers; set direction, raise the technical bar, and manage the team’s health, velocity, and delivery.
Shape the roadmap. Collaborate with Product Management to define and drive the strategy and roadmap for grasping, motion planning and control, perception-for-manipulation, and learned manipulation policies — from research to productized, supported platform capabilities.
Apply creative solutions to real industrial problems. Translate the hardest contact-rich manipulation tasks in manufacturing, logistics, assembly, and machine tending into robust capabilities that work in the real world, not just the lab.
Bridge research and product. Partner with NVIDIA Research, the Isaac Sim/Lab teams, and foundation-model teams (e.g., Isaac GR00T, Cosmos) to bring sim-to-real, imitation, and reinforcement learning approaches into the platform and onto physical arms.
Engage partners and developers. Serve as a technical face of Isaac Manipulation to robot-arm OEMs, system integrators, and the developer community — gathering requirements, running joint engineering, and ensuring our APIs and tools meet real workflows. Support our ecosystem of developers through responsible migration handling of their solutions built on our durable platform.
Leverage accelerated compute. Drive architecture and execution that fully uses NVIDIA GPUs, CUDA, and the accelerated-computing stack across simulation, training, and on-robot inference on Jetson and edge platforms.
Deliver. Drive planning and execution of complex, multi-functional programs; own quality, performance, and the real-world deployment of learned policies and manipulation stacks on physical robots.
Influence the strategy. Represent manipulation in platform-level technical and business decisions, and help shape where NVIDIA invests across the robotics stack.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
12+ total years of relevant industry experience building robotics or robotics-adjacent systems, including 3+ years leading, mentoring, and managing engineering teams.
Robotic arm depth. Hands-on expertise with robotic arms, manipulation, and physics from grasping, motion planning (across both numerical optimization and sampling-based approaches), and control (including force/impedance and contact-rich control) to perception-guided manipulation.
Accelerated compute. Working understanding of GPU-accelerated computing and modern ML infrastructure, and how to architect robotics software to take advantage of it (CUDA, PyTorch, GPU-accelerated simulation, edge inference).
Partner and developer interface. Demonstrated ability to work directly with external partners, customers, and developer communities and to translate their needs into roadmap and shipping product.
Technical credibility. Strong software engineering fundamentals (modern C++ and Python) and the ability to engage substantively in technical and architectural decisions with your team.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Industry leadership and fluency. Experience building manipulation or industrial automation products at an established robot-arm company or manipulation startup, and a strong understanding of the product landscape including use cases, the integrators, and the platforms from leading vendors.
Hardware-agnostic platforms. A track record building developer-facing or low-code platforms and tooling that abstract across multiple robot-arm brands and make manipulation accessible to non-experts.
Learned manipulation. Deep experience with imitation learning, reinforcement learning, sim-to-real transfer, or manipulation foundation models, and shipping learned policies onto real hardware.
Ecosystem & OSS. Contributions to ROS 2, ros2_control, MoveIt, or the broader robotics open-source and standards community.
Founder / 0-to-1 instincts. Experience starting or scaling a product or team from the ground up and operating with speed in ambiguous, fast-pace problem spaces.

Manipulation is one of the defining unsolved problems in robotics, and NVIDIA is uniquely positioned — across simulation, foundation models, and accelerated compute — to solve it at platform scale. You’ll lead a team that the entire robotics industry builds on, and your work will show up on factory floors and in warehouses around the world!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 272,000 USD - 431,250 USD for Level 4, and 320,000 USD - 488,750 USD for Level 5.

Description

AWS Prototyping and AI Customer Engineering (PACE) is the team customers work with when they need to move from idea to production on their most complex AI and cloud challenges. We build working prototypes, run executive briefings, and deliver guided builds that compress months of development into days. Our work directly influences customer commitment decisions spanning generative AI, agentic architectures, computer vision, and full-stack cloud modernization. PACE operates globally with teams aligned to industry verticals in each geo, ensuring deep customer proximity and field stakeholder partnership.

We are looking for a Sr. Manager, Solutions Architecture to lead one of the PACE North America delivery teams, aligned to Financial Services (FSI), Retail & (CPG), and Canada (inclusive of all industries). You will own integrated PODs, each paired with a technical program manager and dedicated prototyping architects, and you will be responsible for the quality, velocity, and business impact of every engagement your team delivers. You will manage approximately 10 to 12 people directly.

You will develop deep relationships with field stakeholders (Sales Directors, Solutions Architecture Leaders, CSM Leaders) across FSI, Retail and CPG, and Canada. You will own the delivery side of those partnerships and drive operational rigor: capacity planning, engagement intake prioritization, prototype quality standards, and the mechanisms that connect prototyping work to launched revenue. You will coach and grow your team across a mix of experience levels, from early-career prototyping architects through senior technical program managers.

The right person for this role has experience building and shipping production-grade AI systems, has led technical teams through ambiguous customer problems, and has the judgment to know when a prototype needs another day of polish and when it needs to ship now. You care about growing people as much as growing the business, and you can context-switch between coaching a newer team member and presenting to a customer CTO in the same afternoon.

Key job responsibilities

Lead, coach, and develop a team of prototyping architects and technical program managers organized in industry-aligned PODs covering FSI, Retail and CPG, and Canada. Own hiring, onboarding, performance management, and promotion readiness for every team member.

Own engagement delivery quality and velocity for your PODs. Set the technical bar for prototypes, executive briefing centers (EBCs), guided builds, and AI Discovery Lifecycle (AI-DLC) workshops. Review architectures and unblock technical decisions across your team's engagements.

Build and maintain deep stakeholder relationships with Sales, SA, and CSM leadership across your industry verticals. Participate in pipeline reviews, strategy sessions, and QBRs. Be the delivery-side counterpart that field leaders call when they need prototyping capacity for a critical account.

Drive operational mechanisms: engagement intake and prioritization, capacity planning and allocation, prototype-to-production tracking, and the reporting that connects delivery to business outcomes. Ensure your PODs are staffed to meet demand without burning out individuals.

Maintain technical currency with GenAI and cloud architecture to sustain credibility with your team and with field stakeholders, particularly in agentic AI (AgentCore, Bedrock Agents), foundation model deployment (SageMaker, EKS), and multi-agent systems.

Partner with peer managers and the PACE North America Leader to balance capacity across verticals during demand spikes, share prototyping assets and patterns across PODs, and maintain a unified quality bar for the organization.

Identify patterns across customer engagements in your verticals and codify them into reusable assets (reference architectures, starter kits, workshop frameworks) that accelerate future delivery and feed the PACE Scale motion.

About The Team

ACE operates at the frontier of what customers are building on AWS. We are the team that takes the hardest "can we actually do this?" questions from the field and turns them into working systems, often in days. Our prototypes have influenced customer commitments across every major industry, displaced competitors in active evaluations, and produced reusable assets now adopted across AWS. We work across every major AI paradigm (generative AI, computer vision, NLP, physical AI, agentic systems) and every major industry vertical in North America.

We are a small, high-output team. That means every person matters, every engagement matters, and the manager closest to the work has real influence on business outcomes. If you want a leadership role where your decisions directly move the needle, this is it.

Knowledge of software development tools and methodologies

Experience working directly with enterprise customers on complex technical engagements, including architecture design, proof-of-concept development, and production deployment.

jobs.title: Chief Information & AI Officer
jobs.description:
Location: hybrid Atlanta, San Diego & Orlando

Full-time, Executive
Reports to the President

Every lender in the country can buy the same AI models on the same afternoon. Almost none of them have worked out how to put those models to work in a business where a wrong answer is a regulatory event — and, for the owner on the other end, a payroll that does not get made. That is the job.

FairSquare is looking for a Chief Information & AI Officer to lead our technology organization — and to build something most companies our size are still only talking about.

You will own the full technology stack: software engineering, data, infrastructure, security and IT. On top of that, you will own a harder question. In a small-business lending company, which work should AI simply do? Which should AI draft, with a named human accountable for the result? And which should never leave human hands at all? Your answer has to hold up three ways at once — for a regulator, for a funding partner, and for the business owner waiting on a decision.

Nobody is going to hand you that answer. You will be the executive who collaborates with the team to define it, builds the operating model and the guardrails that make it real, defends it to the Board and to our regulators and funding partners, and then proves — with evidence, not anecdotes — that it works. You will raise the obstacles early, while they are still cheap to fix, and own the outcome either way.

If you believe the durable advantage in AI belongs to the companies that make it accountable rather than the ones that adopt it first, we should talk.

About FairSquare

FairSquare is a technology-driven financial services company serving small businesses across the United States. We began with a singular focus to bring accessible working capital to our nation’s small businesses and have evolved into a full suite of financial products and the ability to cater to every business need. We combine capital, data and technology to get funding into the hands of business owners quickly and responsibly. Founded in 1999, our subsidiary brands offer a range of diverse financing options from premier small business loans to self-service digital lending platforms that support the needs of our customers throughout every stage of their business journey.

The Role

Reporting directly to the President and serving on the executive leadership team, the Chief Information & AI Officer sets and drives FairSquare’s combined technology and artificial intelligence strategy — ensuring our software, infrastructure and AI systems run efficiently, profitably, securely and responsibly.

This is a builder’s seat, not a caretaker’s. You will make executive technology and AI decisions on behalf of the company: owning the technology and AI budget, aligning investment with our vision and our stakeholders’ needs, sequencing AI use cases against a risk-tiered framework, and uniting software engineering, data science, AI and IT into one team that can actually execute against the strategy you set. You will also lead it the way we expect every leader at FairSquare to lead — commitments owned and delivered on time, problems surfaced before they become surprises, disagreement voiced at the table rather than after the meeting, and full commitment carried forward once a decision is made.

What You Will Do

Set the technology and AI strategy for the enterprise, and keep it tied to our Key Goals and business outcomes rather than to tooling.

Find and deploy the technologies — including AI and machine learning — that create genuine competitive advantage in fintech, and say no to the ones that do not. Curiosity about what is new, discipline about what is worth it.

Stand up and lead an AI Center of Excellence: the central hub that sets standards, shared tooling and playbooks for AI leads embedded across the business — and that spreads what works instead of letting it stay in one team.

Prioritize and sequence AI use cases enterprise-wide against a risk-tiered framework, distinguishing what can be automated outright from what requires human oversight or human judgment alone — and deciding in the customer’s favor when the trade-off is close.

Build the governance that makes speed defensible — model risk management, data protection, quality assurance, fair-lending and regulatory compliance, and explainability and audit standards for AI output.

Own system infrastructure end to end: functionality, resilience, security, and the platforms our AI work depends on.

Define and report the measures that matter — adoption, accuracy, override and correction rates, cycle-time impact and return on investment — and carry that story, good news and bad, to the President and the Board.

Partner across every function to put technology and AI to profitable use: treat internal colleagues as customers, go to the person rather than around them, name the friction you find in a process instead of quietly working around it, and use what you hear back to adjust course.

Coach, develop and retain a distributed team of software, data science, AI and IT professionals — keeping real development plans in place for your leaders and yourself, and working with HR on the AI fluency, reskilling and change management that enterprise AI adoption genuinely requires.

Lead in line with our policies and applicable law: hiring and training, planning and directing work, and developing and rewarding performance.

What You Bring

A bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, data science or a related field; a master’s or PhD in AI/ML is preferred.

At least 10 years in technology roles, including hands-on exposure to AI/ML or data science, and at least 5 years leading people.

A track record of owning budgets and business planning at scale — and of delivering what you committed to, on the date you committed to it.

Strategic range — the ability to set a direction across both the technology and the AI domains, then execute it: consulting widely before you decide, and moving with real urgency once you have.

Deep technical knowledge of cloud platforms, mobile applications and generative AI, and a clear sense of how they apply to financial services and lending.

Real experience with AI governance, model risk management and regulatory compliance — including fair-lending regulation (for example ECOA / Regulation B) and data privacy.

Communication skill that travels: you can explain an AI capability, and its risk, to an engineer and to a director in the same week — and you disagree openly before a decision is made rather than relitigating it afterward.

Leadership and organizational ability across a distributed, cross-functional operating model, with a record of growing people and not only shipping projects — the leaders you have developed are the evidence.

Sound judgment about when AI is the right answer — the confidence to say when it is not, and the self-awareness to name your own blind spots before someone else does.

Why This Role Is Different

Most technology executives inherit a roadmap. You will inherit a mandate.

FairSquare has made a deliberate decision to treat AI as an operating-model question rather than a procurement one — which means the person in this seat gets to redesign how work actually moves through the company, not just buy the software that supports it. Executive leadership and the Board are already engaged and expect to be held to evidence. The budget is real. The scope is the enterprise.

It is also a role with a conscience attached. Every role here touches a customer, and the standard we hold ourselves to is that we can always explain how a decision was made and who was accountable for it. Small businesses risk it all for a dream; we risk it all to make sure they win. If that constraint reads to you as the interesting part of the problem rather than the annoying part, you are the person we are looking for.

Compensation & Location

Salary range: Base Salary: $290K-375K. Position eligible for additional incentives including bonus, equity, 401(k) match, health and welfare benefits, amazing culture, growth opportunity and more.

Location: This position is a Hybrid role and will work from our offices in either: San Diego, CA; Atlanta, GA, or Orlando, FL.

FairSquare is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

We are hiring for a leader for the newly forming Detection and Response team at Plaid. Our mission is to protect Plaid's financial infrastructure by detecting and responding to suspicious activity across the company. We are responsible for the entire lifecycle of detection and response, including detection infrastructure, AI triage and response, investigation tooling, Red Teaming, and Fraud Operations. Security is foundational to the trust thousands of businesses and millions of consumers place in Plaid, and we work directly to reduce risks and enable our business to move faster and safer.

As the Head of Detection and Response, you will be the founding leader responsible for standing up and evaluating Plaid's detection and response team. You will lead a specialized technical team of analysts and engineers, gain deep experience partnering with the CISO and cross-functional engineering leaders, and build critical security infrastructure at scale. This is a unique leadership opportunity to manage a team that encompasses traditional security operations alongside Red Teaming and Fraud Operations, directly impacting Plaid's security posture and long-term stability.

Responsibilities

Form and set up Plaid’s Detection and Response team from scratch, defining its culture and operational standards.
Lead the day-to-day operations for incident response and evaluate the overall effectiveness of the detection and response program.
Manage and mentor a technical team responsible for detection infrastructure, AI-driven triage, and investigation tooling.
Oversee Fraud Operations and Red Team activities to ensure a proactive and comprehensive security posture.
Partner with senior leadership (CISO, CTO, COO) to communicate security risks and maturity gains achieved through influence and cross-functional collaboration.
Define and track metrics to evaluate and demonstrate the effectiveness of the D&R program

Qualifications

Must haves:
8-14 years of overall detection and response or security engineering experience.
Strong technical background in security or detection engineering, with the ability to guide work on SIEMs, EDR, and SOC operations.
Experience managing a team of security analysts and engineers in an operational, platform, or infrastructure context.
Ability to build cross-functional relationships and drive security maturity through influence rather than authority.
High-empathy communication skills with the ability to represent technical work to Staff-level leadership.
Strong AI-first skillset applicable to security operations.

Nice to have:
Experience at a fintech or high-technology organization adjacent to payments/finance.
Background in fraud investigation or software engineering.

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. Product Management at Capital One is a booming, vibrant craft that requires reimagining the status quo, finding value creation opportunities, and driving innovative and sustainable customer experiences through technology. We believe our portfolio of businesses and investments in growth and transformation will result in a company with the scale, brand, capabilities, talent, and values to succeed as the digital revolution transforms our society and our industry.

About The Team

Capital One is looking for an experienced product leader who can lead the Engineering 360 team. This team is optimizing Capital One’s Card developer experience to automate everything but the creative. Creating tooling and best practices to both deliver code faster and, in the background, drive automation that ensures applications are well managed. You will own the strategy and execution of the vision for Capital One’s Card Business; inspire and lead your team, users and adjacent teams; drive a continuous discovery process, optimizing for efficiency and quality. This leader will instill an outcome orientation and partner with product and technology leaders across the organization to deliver exceptional experiences for our developers. One of the most important aspects of the role is building and leading a world-class team to deliver on this journey.

Design the future of a system that ensures applications are well managed while optimizing developers’ time towards application development.
Work with leaders across the company to find and take advantage of valuable shared services, allowing your team more time to focus on unique, high-value work
Delve into microservice and cloud-native architecture to decouple business strategy changes from underlying transaction processing logic, increasing speed to market and reducing risk
Drive accelerated continuous discovery process that optimizes on user adoption through outcome orientation and empowerment
Deliver value to the Card business and its customers by accelerating innovation and engineer enablement

Human Centered - Obsesses about internal and external customer needs to reimagine and innovate product solutions
Business Focused - Delivers game-changing outcomes by focusing on leverage and execution excellence

Transformational Leadership - Leads cross functional teams to solve customer problems and drive organizational alignment

Experience translating business strategy and analysis into consumer facing digital products

jobs.description:
Overview

Microsoft AI Experiences (AIX) is building the future of AI experiences across Copilot, Bing, Edge, and partner surfaces that reach hundreds of millions of people.

As AI products grow in reach and sophistication, access to compute and infrastructure is increasingly central to product strategy, customer experience, and business performance. We are looking for a strategic and analytical leader to shape how AIX plans, allocates, and manages the infrastructure that powers our AI experiences.

This role sits within the AIX Strategy organization and will lead cross-functional planning and decision-making for GPU capacity and related infrastructure investments. Working across Product, Engineering, Finance, and Infrastructure teams, you will develop forecasting models, establish resource-allocation frameworks, drive infrastructure governance, and ensure capacity investments are aligned to business priorities and product outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines strong strategic thinking, quantitative rigor, business judgment, and operational excellence. They are equally comfortable discussing infrastructure constraints with engineering teams, evaluating business tradeoffs with finance partners, and presenting recommendations to senior executives.

AI Experiences employees who live within a 50- mile commute of a designated Microsoft Hub in the U.S. are expected to work from the office at least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.

Responsibilities

Lead forecasting and planning for GPU capacity and other AI infrastructure resources across AIX.
Develop demand models that incorporate product roadmaps, user growth, model transitions, workload characteristics, and migration plans.
Create and maintain frameworks for evaluating, prioritizing, and allocating constrained infrastructure resources across products and business priorities.
Drive governance processes for infrastructure requests, allocation decisions, escalations, and executive reviews.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, and Finance teams to connect infrastructure investments to business outcomes, including engagement, quality, revenue, efficiency, and customer experience.
Build quantitative models, scenario analyses, and business cases to support investment and resource-allocation decisions.
Define and improve the telemetry, reporting, and dashboards required to understand infrastructure utilization, capacity, throttling, costs, and business impact.
Lead cross-organizational initiatives involving infrastructure migrations, workload transitions, capacity reallocations, and cost-optimization efforts.
Identify capacity risks early and develop mitigation strategies that preserve business objectives while improving efficiency.
Translate complex technical and operational information into clear recommendations and executive-ready communications.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Master's Degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or related field AND 6+ years experience in strategy, business planning, finance, product management, operations, or program management,
OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or related field AND 8+ years of experience in strategy, business planning, finance, product management, operations, program management
OR equivalent experience.

6+ years of experience with AI infrastructure, cloud capacity planning, model serving, inference, training, or distributed systems.
6+ years of experience building business cases and ROI models for technology investments.
6+ years of experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Finance organizations.
6+ years of experience with SQL, Python, Power BI, Kusto, Excel, or other analytical tools.
Experience operating in fast-paced, highly ambiguous environments and creating structure where processes do not yet exist.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's Degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or related field AND 12+ years of experience in strategy, business planning, finance, product management, operations, or program management
6+ years experience in Strategy, Management Consulting, and/or Finance.
6+ years of experience with AI infrastructure, cloud capacity planning, model serving, inference, training, or distributed systems.
Experience building business cases and ROI models for technology investments.
Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Finance organizations.
Experience with SQL, Python, Power BI, Kusto, Excel, or other analytical tools.
Experience operating in fast-paced, highly ambiguous environments and creating structure where processes do not yet exist.
